description: If total assets are $80000 and total equity is $35000 what are total liabilities?
explanation: Using the accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Equity

description: Which of the following transactions would include a debit to Cash?
explanation: When a customer pays on account (cash collected on accounts receivable)
hint: Cash is debited because the asset increases. All other options would credit Cash.
choice3: Collecting cash from a customer on account

description: If current assets are $60000 and current liabilities are $20000, what is the current ratio?
explanation: The current ratio = Current Assets / Current Liabilities = $60000 / $20000 = 3.0. A ratio above 1 means the company has more current assets than current liabilities, indicating good short-term liquidity.
hint: Current Ratio = Current Assets / Current Liabilities

description: Which journal entry records the payment of salaries owed that were previously accrued?
explanation: Salaries were previously accrued by debiting Salaries Expense and crediting Salaries Payable. When paid
hint: the liability (Salaries Payable) is debited to eliminate it and Cash is credited.
choice3: Debit Salaries Expense, Credit Salaries Payable

description: Under the FIFO inventory method when prices are rising which result is correct?
explanation: Under FIFO (First-In First-Out) the oldest (lowest cost) inventory is sold first during periods of rising prices. This means COGS is lower and ending inventory value is higher compared to LIFO.
choice0: Higher COGS and lower ending inventory
choice1: Lower COGS and higher ending inventory

description: The net realizable value of accounts receivable equals?
explanation: Net realizable value (NRV) is the amount of accounts receivable the company actually expects to collect. It equals gross accounts receivable minus the allowance for doubtful accounts.
choice0: Gross accounts receivable minus sales discounts
choice1: Total credit sales minus cash collected
choice2: Gross accounts receivable minus allowance for doubtful accounts

description: A company buys equipment for $10000 with a salvage value of $2000 and a 4-year life. What is straight-line annual depreciation?
explanation: Straight-line depreciation = (Cost - Salvage Value) / Useful Life = ($10000 - $2000) / 4 = $8000 / 4 = $2000 per year.

description: Which of the following would increase gross profit without changing net sales?
explanation: Lower cost of goods sold (COGS) increases gross profit because Gross Profit = Net Sales - COGS. If COGS decreases while sales stay the same

description: Which of the following best describes working capital?
explanation: Working capital = Current Assets - Current Liabilities. It measures the short-term liquidity of a company - whether it can cover its short-term obligations with its short-term resources.

description: An accrued expense is best described as?
explanation: An accrued expense is one that has been incurred (the benefit has been received) but not yet paid. It creates a liability (accrued expense payable) at the end of the period before cash payment occurs.
choice0: An expense paid before it is incurred
choice1: An expense recorded when cash is paid
choice2: An expense incurred but not yet paid
choice3: A prepaid expense used during the period

description: If a company debits Accounts Receivable and credits Revenue what type of transaction occurred?
explanation: Debiting Accounts Receivable and crediting Revenue records a sale on credit. The company earned revenue but has not yet received cash - the customer owes money.
choice1: Cash was collected from a customer
choice3: An asset was purchased on credit

description: A company performs services in December but receives payment in January. Under accrual accounting revenue is recorded in?
explanation: Under accrual accounting revenue is recognized when earned - when the service is performed - not when payment is received. So revenue is recorded in December when the service was provided.
choice1: February at the next accounting period
choice3: December when the service is performed

description: Which of the following items appears on the statement of cash flows but NOT on the income statement?
explanation: Depreciation appears as an add-back on the cash flow statement (indirect method) but is an expense on the income statement. Wait - actually depreciation IS on both. Capital expenditures appear only on the investing section of the cash flow statement

description: The materiality principle allows companies to?
explanation: The materiality principle states that insignificant items may be treated in the most practical manner. For immaterial (trivial) amounts
hint: strict adherence to GAAP is not required since the impact on financial statements is negligible.
choice1: Omit major items from financial statements
choice2: Record assets at market value rather than cost
choice3: Expense minor items immediately even if they technically should be capitalized
column15: Defer all expenses to future periods

description: When merchandise is purchased on account the journal entry is?
explanation: Purchasing merchandise on account increases Inventory (an asset - debit) and creates an obligation to pay (Accounts Payable - credit the liability).

description: A company has net income of $30000 and net sales of $150000. What is the net profit margin?
explanation: Net Profit Margin = Net Income / Net Sales = $30000 / $150000 = 0.20 or 20%. This measures how many cents of profit are generated for each dollar of sales.
hint: Net Profit Margin = Net Income / Net Sales

description: Treasury stock (shares repurchased by the company) appears on the balance sheet as?
explanation: Treasury stock is a contra-equity account. It reduces stockholders equity because the company bought back its own shares. It is listed as a deduction within the equity section of the balance sheet.

description: What is the journal entry to record depreciation expense?
explanation: Depreciation reduces the value of an asset and creates an expense. You debit Depreciation Expense (increases the expense) and credit Accumulated Depreciation (a contra-asset that reduces the book value of the asset).
choice2: Debit Depreciation Expense, Credit Accumulated Depreciation
choice3: Debit Accumulated Depreciation, Credit Depreciation Expense

description: At year-end a company owes $5000 in interest that has not been paid. What entry is required?
explanation: An interest obligation that exists but has not been paid is an accrued liability. You debit Interest Expense (recognizing the expense in the current period) and credit Interest Payable (the liability).
choice0: Debit Interest Expense, Credit Interest Payable

description: Accumulated depreciation on the balance sheet is classified as?
explanation: Accumulated Depreciation is a contra-asset account. It is listed on the balance sheet as a deduction from the related asset (like equipment) to show the net book value (cost minus accumulated depreciation).

description: Which inventory method assumes the most recently purchased goods are sold first?
explanation: LIFO stands for Last-In First-Out. It assumes the most recently purchased (last in) inventory is sold first. This is the opposite of FIFO (First-In First-Out).

description: A company pays $12000 on January 1 for a 12-month insurance policy. Under accrual accounting how much insurance expense is recorded in January?
explanation: Under accrual accounting the $12000 prepayment creates a prepaid asset. Only 1 month of coverage (1 / 12 of $12000 = $1000) is used in January so only $1000 is recognized as expense in January.

description: Bad debt expense is recorded under the allowance method when?
explanation: Under the allowance method bad debt expense is estimated and recorded at the end of each period - before any specific account is identified as uncollectible. This matches the expense with the revenue period. When a specific account is written off it affects the allowance not the expense.
choice0: An estimate of uncollectible accounts is made at period end
choice1: A specific customer account is written off
choice2: A customer pays a previously written-off account

description: If a company has total debt of $200000 and total equity of $400000, what is the debt-to-equity ratio?
explanation: Debt-to-Equity Ratio = Total Debt / Total Equity = $200000 / $400000 = 0.5. This ratio measures the proportion of financing that comes from creditors versus owners.

description: Intangible assets include which of the following?
explanation: Intangible assets are non-physical long-term assets with economic value. Patents and trademarks are intangible assets. Equipment and buildings are tangible assets. Accounts receivable is a current asset.

description: When a company issues common stock for cash the journal entry is?
explanation: Issuing stock for cash increases Cash (an asset - debit) and increases Common Stock and/or Additional Paid-in Capital (equity accounts - credit).

description: On a multi-step income statement what appears between gross profit and operating income?
explanation: On a multi-step income statement: Net Sales - COGS = Gross Profit; Gross Profit - Operating Expenses = Operating Income. Operating expenses (selling and administrative) appear between gross profit and operating income.

description: Deferred (unearned) revenue arises when?
explanation: Deferred revenue is created when a company receives cash before it earns the revenue by performing the service or delivering the product. It is a liability until the obligation is fulfilled.
choice0: A company records revenue before the sale is made
choice1: A customer has not yet paid for services performed
choice2: An expense is paid in advance
choice3: Cash is received before the service is performed

description: A company receives a $500 utility bill but does not pay it immediately. What is the correct journal entry?
explanation: Receiving a utility bill creates an expense (Utilities Expense is debited) and a liability (Accounts Payable or Utilities Payable is credited) because the company owes the amount.
choice1: Debit Utilities Expense, Credit Accounts Payable
choice2: Debit Utilities Payable, Credit Utilities Expense

description: Which depreciation method results in higher depreciation expense in the early years of an asset's life?
explanation: The double-declining-balance method is an accelerated method that applies twice the straight-line rate to the book value. This results in higher depreciation in earlier years and lower depreciation in later years.

description: A company has gross profit of $90000 and net sales of $300000. What is the gross profit margin?
explanation: Gross Profit Margin = Gross Profit / Net Sales = $90000 / $300000 = 0.30 or 30%. It measures profitability before operating expenses are deducted.
hint: Gross Profit Margin = Gross Profit / Net Sales

description: Which of the following is classified as a financing activity on the cash flow statement?
explanation: Borrowing money by issuing a note payable is a financing activity because it involves obtaining funds from creditors. Buying equipment is investing. Collecting from customers and paying suppliers are operating activities.
choice3: Borrowing money by issuing a note payable

description: Under the weighted average cost method inventory cost is calculated as?
explanation: The weighted average cost method calculates an average cost per unit by dividing total cost of goods available for sale by the total number of units available. This average cost is then applied to units sold and units remaining.
choice0: Cost of the first units purchased
choice1: Cost of the last units purchased
choice2: Total cost divided by total units available

description: The full disclosure principle requires that?
explanation: The full disclosure principle requires that financial statements include all information necessary for users to make informed decisions. This includes notes to financial statements that explain accounting policies and significant events.
choice0: All transactions be recorded in real time
choice2: All material information that could affect decisions be disclosed in financial statements
choice3: Companies report detailed information about every employee

description: Which of the following is classified as a long-term (non-current) asset?
explanation: Property (land and buildings) is a long-term asset used in operations over many years. Cash is a current asset. Accounts receivable and inventory are also current assets expected to be converted to cash within one year.

description: To close revenue accounts at the end of the period you would?
explanation: Temporary accounts (revenues
calculator: dividends) are closed at period-end. To close a revenue account with a credit balance you debit the revenue account and credit Income Summary to zero it out.
choice2: Debit Income Summary, Credit Retained Earnings

description: When a company takes advantage of a purchase discount the cash paid is?
explanation: A purchase discount reduces the amount paid for inventory. If a company buys $5000 of inventory with terms 2 / 10
calculator: paying within 10 days means paying $5000 x 0.98 = $4900
choice3: Equal to the full invoice price
column15: Less than the full invoice price
column16: More than the full invoice price
column17: The same regardless of when payment is made

description: A prepaid expense is initially recorded as?
explanation: When an expense is paid in advance it is recorded as an asset (prepaid expense) because it represents a future economic benefit. As time passes and the benefit is consumed the prepaid is converted to an expense.

description: Under a single-step income statement all revenues are grouped together and then?
explanation: A single-step income statement groups all revenues together and all expenses together. Total revenues minus total expenses = net income. This is simpler than the multi-step format but shows less detail about profitability.
choice0: All expenses are deducted in one step to get net income
choice2: Operating and non-operating items are separated
choice3: Cost of goods sold is subtracted first

description: If accounts receivable is $50000 and net credit sales are $300000, what is the accounts receivable turnover?
explanation: Accounts Receivable Turnover = Net Credit Sales / Average Accounts Receivable = $300000 / $50000 = 6. This means the company collects its average receivables balance 6 times per year.
hint: AR Turnover = Net Credit Sales / Accounts Receivable

description: Under straight-line depreciation the book value of an asset at the end of its useful life should equal?
explanation: Under straight-line depreciation the asset is depreciated down to its estimated salvage (residual) value by the end of its useful life. The book value at that point equals the salvage value.

description: In the indirect method of preparing the operating section of the cash flow statement depreciation is?
explanation: Depreciation is a non-cash expense that was deducted on the income statement to arrive at net income. To reconcile net income to operating cash flows we add depreciation back because no cash was actually paid.
choice1: Added to net income only if it exceeds $1000

description: A company pays a $3000 dividend to shareholders. How does this affect the accounting equation?
explanation: Dividends reduce retained earnings (equity decreases) and reduce cash (asset decreases). The equation remains balanced because both sides decrease by the same amount.

description: Which accounting principle supports recording an asset at its original cost rather than its inflated current value?
explanation: The cost principle (historical cost) requires that assets be recorded and reported at their original acquisition cost. This provides a reliable and verifiable basis for financial reporting.

description: A company debits Rent Expense and credits Prepaid Rent. What accounting event occurred?
explanation: Crediting Prepaid Rent reduces the asset (the prepaid has been used up). Debiting Rent Expense records the cost of the period used. This is an adjusting entry to recognize rent expense as prepaid coverage expires.
choice1: Prepaid rent was used up and expensed
choice3: Future rent was paid in advance

description: Which of the following would be found in the stockholders equity section of a balance sheet?
explanation: Retained Earnings is part of stockholders equity representing cumulative net income less dividends. Notes Payable is a liability. Accounts Receivable is an asset. Unearned Revenue is a liability.

description: Which inventory costing method is NOT permitted under IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards)?
explanation: LIFO (Last-In First-Out) is prohibited under IFRS because it can distort inventory values and income. FIFO
calculator: and Specific Identification are all acceptable under IFRS.

description: Which basis of accounting better matches revenues with the expenses incurred to earn them?
explanation: Accrual basis accounting records revenues when earned and expenses when incurred regardless of cash flow. This provides a better matching of revenues and expenses than the cash basis.

description: When a specific customer account is written off under the allowance method the entry is?
explanation: Writing off a specific account reduces Accounts Receivable and reduces the Allowance for Doubtful Accounts. Bad Debt Expense is NOT recorded at write-off under the allowance method - it was already estimated earlier.
choice0: Debit Bad Debt Expense, Credit Accounts Receivable
choice1: Debit Allowance for Doubtful Accounts, Credit Accounts Receivable
choice2: Debit Accounts Receivable, Credit Allowance for Doubtful Accounts
choice3: Debit Bad Debt Expense, Credit Allowance for Doubtful Accounts

description: A company purchases land for $75000 cash. How does this transaction affect the accounting equation?
explanation: Buying land for cash swaps one asset (cash) for another asset (land). Total assets remain the same. Neither liabilities nor equity are affected.
choice2: Assets are unchanged (one asset replaces another)

description: Which of the following would be classified as other income (non-operating income) on the income statement?
explanation: Interest income earned on investments is non-operating income because it does not come from the company's core business operations. Sales revenue
calculator: and operating expenses are all part of operating income calculations.
